title: Scalar comparison preserves the specified integral and rational shifts
statement: Fix a prime ell, an algebraic closure Omega/Q_ell, finite subextensions E≤L and a scheme isomorphism g:X→Y with ell invertible [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Specify integral and rational shifts for the pullbacks at E and L. For each endpoint suppose that an inverse-image comparison has the prescribed inverseImagePullbackComparisonDerived components and commutes with the integral shift, and that the rational degree-one comparison is localization of the integral one. Let alpha be any integral natural isomorphism whose components are exactly integralPullbackScalarComparison [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Then alpha commutes with the two specified integral shifts and the canonical integral transition shifts. The already prescribed rationalPullbackScalarComparison commutes with the specified rational pullback shifts and canonical rational transition shifts. No stages, exactness, standard-half preservation, or coherence equations are concluded.

source.place: Proof, final sentence on automorphism pullback: completed-to-termwise comparison, t-exactness, and rational scalar/shift coherence (previous steps 8-9); agent extraction of the existing corrected stage-1 argument, not a quoted theorem of the blueprint

proof.text: Apply the proved integral normalization-and-conjugation lemma to the specified sE, sL, eE, eL and alpha. Its hypotheses are exactly the integral part of the hypotheses here. No rational shift structure is needed for this step.

Use the normalized object and pure-tensor map formulas for rational pullback and rational scalar extension, the fixed rational triangulation datum, and the specified degree-one equations hrE and hrL to transport the two composite shift components through rationalization. The prescribed rational scalar comparison has component Q_L(alpha). Thus its degree-one square is the image under Q_L of the integral square.

A degree-one CommShiftCore equation implies the equations in all integer degrees: use the addition law for positive integers; faithfulness of the shift functor and the inverse shift-addition isomorphisms give the negative-degree equation. Apply integer induction and CommShift.of_core. All shifts and comparisons remain the ones specified in the statement.

    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    (hX : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (l : X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hY : ∀ y : Y, IsUnit (l : Y.presheaf.stalk y))
    (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L)

      NatTrans.CommShift eE.hom ℤ) (_s := sE))
    (hrE : ∀ K, HEq (((rationalDerivedPullback l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) g).commShiftIso (self
      := rE) (1 : ℤ)).hom.app
        ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) Y).obj K))

      : ℤ)).hom.app K)))
    (sL : (constructibleIntegralPullback l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) g).CommShift ℤ)
    (rL : (rationalDerivedPullback l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) g).CommShift ℤ)
    (eL : (sfIntegralConstructible l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) Y).ι ⋙ inverseImageIntegralDerived

      (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) X).ι)
    (heL : ∀ K, HEq (eL.hom.app K)
      (inverseImagePullbackComparisonDerived l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) g hX hY K.obj))
    (hsL : (fun [_s : (constructibleIntegralPullback l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) g).CommShift ℤ] ↦
      NatTrans.CommShift eL.hom ℤ) (_s := sL))
    (hrL : ∀ K, HEq (((rationalDerivedPullback l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) g).commShiftIso (self
      := rL) (1 : ℤ)).hom.app
        ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) Y).obj K))
      ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) X).map
      (((constructibleIntegralPullback l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) g).commShiftIso (self := sL) (1

      @NatTrans.CommShift _ _ _ _ _ _
        (rationalPullbackScalarComparison l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L)
